What the leak allegedly contains: * Ponta member IDs * Full names, emails and phone numbers * Postal codes and street addresses * Transaction history with partner names, amounts and points balances  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If authentic, names, contact details and real purchase history would let fraudsters send very convincing phishing and points-theft lures to members. The total record count has not been stated, and samples like this can come from a partner or analytics export rather than core systems. No official confirmation that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Japan #Ponta #DataBreach #LoyaltyProgram #ThreatIntelligence

🇸🇦 🚨 SAUDI ARABIA: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS LEAK OF 3.6GB OF MINISTRY OF DEFENSE DOCUMENTS  A threat actor on a leak forum has published what they claim is a 3.6GB dump of secret documents from Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense. The files are being shared for download through third-party file-hosting and messaging links.  What the dump allegedly contains: * Internal notices and circulars * Records of private meetings * Images of official documents * Screenshots of WhatsApp conversations  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If authentic, internal military notices and staff chats could expose personnel, operations and internal processes, and would be useful for targeted phishing and espionage. Dumps like this often mix old, public or fabricated material with real files, and the WhatsApp images could come from a single compromised phone rather than ministry systems. The ministry has not confirmed an incident that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #SaudiArabia #MinistryOfDefense #Military #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence

🇺🇿 🚨 UZBEKISTAN PROBES REPORTED LEAK OF CITIZENS' ID AND VEHICLE DATA  Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry says it has opened a joint review with the State Security Service's Cybersecurity Center after databases said to hold citizens' personal data began circulating in Telegram bots on Oct. 28-29.  • Users report PINFL personal ID numbers, passport details, home addresses, phone numbers, vehicle plates, driving licence and vehicle registration data • Posts link the records to SAFE Service (formerly SafeRoad, the traffic-fine app run with the ministry's traffic police), inDrive, Lada Auto, KiwiTaxi and Fargo • SAFE Service denies any leak, saying the records were compiled from various sources before its app launched  ⚠️ Analyst Note: No breach has been confirmed. The origin of the data, the number of people affected and any link to the named services remain unverified. Aggregated "probiv" lookup bots often merge older leaks, so treat this as a combined-dataset exposure claim until the ministry reports its findings.  Research date: Oct 29-30, 2026 reports (reviewed Nov 3). kun.uz/en/news/2026/10/30/in… #DDW #CyberSecurity #Uzbekistan #DataLeak

🇯🇵 🚨 SEGA SERVER INTRUSION DISRUPTS ALL.NET AND AIME ARCADE SERVICES  SEGA FAVE says a third party gained unauthorized access to internal servers tied to ALL.Net, its arcade game network, and the Aime card system. It suspended related services from 3:00 PM JST on Nov. 1, 2026, while it investigates.  • Suspended: online play for ALL.Net titles, Aime card play, PrizeON play, SEGA Lucky Kuji Online and new SEGA ID sign-ups • Bandai Namco's support notice confirms disruption to its own ALL.Net-supported titles, with no restart time given • SEGA says its initial investigation found no exfiltration of customer or partner data, and payment card data is kept on separate systems  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Bandai Namco's notice confirms service impact only, not the intrusion details. No actor, ransomware claim or CVE has been disclosed, and the data-theft finding is preliminary. One shared arcade network carries the outage beyond a single publisher.  sega.jp/important_infos/deta… #DDW #SEGA #Gaming #CyberSecurity

🇧🇷 🚨 MERCADO BITCOIN THEFT ESTIMATED AT ~$49M; ABOUT $10M FROZEN  Incident responder Chainalysis says an attacker drained an estimated $49 million from Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest crypto exchange, in the early hours of Nov. 2, 2026.  • Assets were swept in waves across 17 blockchains, with the largest tranches in Bitcoin and Ethereum and smaller amounts on Base, Tron and Polygon • The exchange shared its list of unauthorized transactions with Chainalysis around 2:30 AM ET on Nov. 2 • Working with law enforcement and stablecoin issuers, investigators helped freeze nearly $10M, including more than $9M in USDT frozen by Tether • Tracing of the remaining funds continues  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The ~$49M figure is the responder's estimate, not an audited loss, and Chainalysis is an incident-response participant working for the exchange. Freezes are not the same as funds returned to the exchange. The access route and the attacker have not been disclosed. This updates our earlier report of a precautionary deposit and withdrawal pause.  chainalysis.com/blog/chainal… #DDW #MercadoBitcoin #Crypto #CyberSecurity

🇺🇸 🚨 WORKOS CONFIRMS BREACH OF INTERNAL SALES TOOL; CRM AND SUPPORT DATA ACCESSED  Identity-infrastructure vendor WorkOS says it found unauthorized access on Oct. 30 to an internal application used by its sales and customer-facing teams.  • Accessed data includes business contacts (names, emails, phone numbers, job titles), account histories, and summaries and excerpts of sales calls, support chats and customer Slack conversations • Operational metadata about customers' product usage and connection or directory health was also exposed • WorkOS disabled external access to the tool and retained an outside forensics firm; per-customer impact is still under review • The company says attackers used an AI-assisted offensive framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts  ⚠️ Analyst Note: WorkOS says it has no evidence that application data or production services were accessed. No victim count or exfiltration volume has been disclosed, and the AI-assisted attribution is the company's own assessment. Real conversation details make follow-on phishing more convincing, so verify unexpected requests that cite past WorkOS contacts.  workos.com/security/bulletin… #DDW #WorkOS #DataBreach #CyberSecurity

🇯🇵 🚨 UPDATE: JAPAN'S ARARA BREACH EXPANDS TO ~77M EMAIL ADDRESSES ACROSS UP TO 380 CLIENT COMPANIES  Email-delivery provider Arara's Nov. 2 second report says attackers also reached client-company environments on 97 servers, beyond the shared environment it disclosed on Oct. 29.  • About 77M email addresses taken or possibly taken; the count is still being refined and is not a count of unique people • Data can include names, gender, birth dates, phone numbers, member IDs and addresses, depending on the client; Arara says it holds no card numbers • Attackers also abused the service to send up to ~7.13M phishing emails posing as credit-card companies (messages, not extra victims) • All "Arara Message" service has been suspended since Oct. 31, with no restart date • Customer SMT Members corrected its earlier no-impact notice: members' email addresses leaked  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Do not add 77M to the earlier figure. Arara revised the shared-environment count to ~3.39M unique addresses and does not sum the categories because of overlap. It links the attacks to the same third party; no actor, CVE or ransomware group is named. Expect phishing aimed at affected addresses.  arara.com/dcms_media/other/a… #DDW #Japan #Arara #DataBreach #EmailSecurity

🇲🇽 🏦 MEXICO: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS SALE OF ALLEGED BANCOPPEL CUSTOMER DATABASE  A threat actor on an underground forum is advertising what they claim is a customer database stolen from BanCoppel, the Mexican bank linked to the Coppel retail group. The seller is taking buyers through an escrow service. No record count was given.  What the data allegedly contains: * Full names and physical addresses * CURP and tax identifiers * Phone numbers * Credit limits and Coppel credit product details  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If real, national ID numbers combined with credit details and phone numbers are ideal for identity fraud and bank-impersonation calls or SMS. BanCoppel customers should treat unexpected contact about their accounts or credit with caution and reach the bank only through official channels. The bank has not confirmed an incident that we are aware of. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #DataBreach #Mexico #Banking #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 HPE ARUBAOS: 8 CVSS 10.0 UNAUTHENTICATED RCE / AUTH BYPASS FLAWS IN AOS-8 AND AOS-10  HPE released advisory HPESBNW05162 on Oct 22, 2026, fixing 72 vulnerabilities in the wireless operating systems that run Aruba Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways and Access Points.  What's reported: • 8 maximum-severity flaws (CVE-2026-79844 to CVE-2026-79851): authentication bypass, command injection, SQL injection and buffer overflows leading to remote code execution, with no login needed • Affected: AOS-10.8.1.1, 10.7.2.6, 10.4.1.13, AOS-8.13.3.0, 8.10.0.23 and below • Fixed in AOS-10 10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7, 10.4.1.14 and AOS-8 8.13.3.1, 8.10.0.24 • HPE says it is not aware of public exploit code or discussion yet  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Wireless controllers sit at the core of enterprise networks, so a pre-auth RCE here is a direct path to the internal network. Patch now, and until then restrict CLI, web management and PAPI access to a dedicated management VLAN or firewall-controlled segment. End-of-maintenance releases are presumed affected.  Source: support.hpe.com/hpesc/public… #DDW #DarkWeb #HPE #Aruba #CVE #RCE #PatchNow #CyberSecurity

🇦🇺 🚨 AUSTRALIA: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS TO SELL ~1M MYHAIRCARE CUSTOMER RECORDS  A threat actor on an underground forum is offering a database they say was taken from MyHairCare, an Australian online hair-care retailer.  The actor claims the data includes: * About 1,048,576 customer records * Last names, email addresses and phone numbers * City, postcode, province and country * Total amount spent, currency and email-verification status  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The exact count matches a spreadsheet's maximum row limit, so the export may be truncated or padded. Even so, contact and spend data like this fuels targeted phishing and fake refund scams. MyHairCare has not confirmed an incident. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #MyHairCare #DataBreach #Australia #ThreatIntelligence

🇰🇷 🚨 SOUTH KOREA: 12.1 MILLION CJ CGV CUSTOMER RECORDS ALLEGEDLY OFFERED FOR SALE  A threat actor is advertising a database of 12.1 million records allegedly taken from CJ CGV, South Korea's largest cinema chain, for just $250 on a dark web forum.  The actor claims the data includes: * User IDs, full names, phone numbers and email addresses * Physical addresses * Ticket booking history and booking status * Payment details such as gross and net amounts paid  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The sample's booking and payment fields point to an export from a customer or ticketing database. At that low price the data could spread quickly, raising the risk of smishing and phishing that impersonates CGV. CJ CGV has not confirmed an incident. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #SouthKorea #Entertainment #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence

🇪🇸 🚨 SPAIN: HT MÉDICA PATIENT DATABASE WITH 2.2 MILLION RECORDS ALLEGEDLY FOR SALE  A threat actor using the name SpartanX is selling a database they claim holds 2.2 million records from HT Médica (Health Time), a Spanish diagnostic imaging provider.  The actor claims the data includes: * First and last names, birth dates and sex * DNI (Spanish national ID) numbers * Email addresses, personal and work phone numbers * Home addresses, postal codes and cities  ⚠️ Analyst Note: National ID numbers tied to patient contact details create a serious risk of identity theft and of phishing that impersonates the clinic or health insurers. If confirmed, the incident would fall under GDPR breach notification rules. HT Médica has not confirmed an incident. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Spain #Healthcare #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence

🇷🇺 RUSSIA'S EMERGENCY-MINISTRY APP SENT FALSE NUCLEAR WARNINGS  False nuclear warnings reached users of Russia's emergency-ministry (MCHS) app.  The ministry says a cyberattack enabled bogus messages and that remediation work was underway. Local outlet 59.RU independently reports recipients in Perm and shows the false alert.  The incident illustrates how compromised public-notification services can spread dangerous misinformation. The attacker and access route remain unverified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This concerns the mobile app, not a verified compromise of Russia's siren network or all emergency channels. No evidence links it to the separate Ukrainian alert-app incident. Ministry-reported remediation is not independently verified recovery.  42.mchs.gov.ru/deyatelnost/p… #Cybersecurity #Russia

🇨🇳 🚨 CHINA: 401 MILLION CTRIP CUSTOMER RECORDS ALLEGEDLY OFFERED FOR SALE  A threat actor on a dark web forum is selling a dataset of 401 million records they claim came from Ctrip (Trip.com Group), China's largest online travel platform. The asking price is $1,500 in crypto.  The actor claims the data includes: * Full names, phone numbers and street addresses * User IDs, account status and registration dates * Hotel, rail and flight booking counts and booking history * Upcoming departure dates and payment totals  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Fields such as last booking and next departure suggest fairly recent data, which would make travel-themed phishing and booking scams far more convincing. The 401M figure may include duplicates or older aggregated data. Ctrip has not confirmed an incident. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #China #Travel #DataBreach #ThreatIntelligence

🇮🇶 🚨 IRAQ: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS TO LEAK 2026 KIRKUK RESIDENCY DATABASE  A threat actor on an underground forum has posted what it calls a sample from the 2026 Kirkuk residency database.  The listing claims the records include: * Full names, mothers' names, date and place of birth, gender * Phone numbers and full addresses (district, sub-district, neighborhood, house number) * National ID, civil status ID and residency card numbers * Marital status, spouse details and number of children * Minority-group membership, special needs and "martyr family" status  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If genuine, this is a highly sensitive civil-registry dataset. Kirkuk is an ethnically mixed, politically contested province, and fields flagging minority status and "martyr" families could expose residents to targeting, identity fraud and SIM-swap scams. No Iraqi authority has confirmed an incident, and the record count and the system it came from are unknown. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach.  Source: this is for subscribers only. Subscribe: nitter.mie.foundation/DailyDarkWeb/creator-s… #DDW #DarkWeb #Iraq #Kirkuk #Government #DataLeak #PII #ThreatIntelligence

🇵🇪 🚨 PERU: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS LEAK OF PROYECTO ESPECIAL CHAVIMOCHIC DATABASE  A threat actor on a dark web forum claims to have published a database belonging to Proyecto Especial CHAVIMOCHIC (PECH), the La Libertad regional government's irrigation and hydraulic infrastructure project that also supplies water to Trujillo, Peru.  According to the actor: * More than 100,000 records were exfiltrated from the agency * The data allegedly includes personal records and contact information * Project details and administrative documents are also claimed  The forum post itself shows only the thread title ("DATABASE PROYECTO CHAVIMOCHIC GOB[.]PE") and a skull banner, with no sample rows or field list visible.  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: PECH runs dams, canals and water supply for one of Peru's largest agricultural regions, so staff, contractor, landholder and procurement records could be involved, enabling targeted phishing and fraud against people linked to the project. The poster is a new forum account and no sample has been shown, so the volume and contents remain unconfirmed. Peruvian public bodies are frequent targets of leak claims. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a breach of Proyecto Especial CHAVIMOCHIC.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Peru #Chavimochic #LaLibertad #Government #WaterUtility #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence

sample_tweets.text: Update on the 9.8 CVSS TCP/IP RCE in the Linux kernel (CVE-2026-98432): we've detected what appears to be a threat actor activity scanning the entire internet for exposed affected systems. Our own scanning also suggests that the number of potential targets is high, therefore there is an increased likelihood of threat actors attempting to develop exploits for the vulnerability.  while CVE-2026-98432 is believed to require MPTCP to be enabled in the kernel, as well as a listening app/service which binds an MPTCP socket, which many have suggested should be rare, several kernels including Debian enable MPTCP by default.  Additionally, Go 1.24+ binds MPTCP sockets by default if the option is enabled in the kernel, so anything built on top of Go (including Caddy) will create the required MPTCP listener.  The mitigation of setting net.mptcp.enabled=0 disabled MPTCP, but does not apply to existing sockets, so any applications that have bound MPTCP sockets need to be restarted, otherwise the system remains exploitable.  You can check if your server is running any MPTCP listeners with the following command: sudo ss -Mlnp  On 2026-10-30 our preliminary internet-wide scan of port 443 confirmed that there are approximately 2,102,043 servers that are successfully reachable via an MPTCP connection. A deeper scan which attempts to connect to each endpoint on port 443 and negotiate a full TLS connection with MPTCP enabled returned about 762,774 systems.  Neither scan can confirm that these are unpatched kernels, just total exposure, but it's a lot more systems than expected. Since a valid HTTP connection is not required to exploit the vulnerability, the total attack surface is likely closer to the 2.1 million number than the 763k one.  As of today (2026-11-02), we've picked up several residential proxies and VPNs scanning the internet on port 443 using MPTCP-enabled connections. Since regular scanners do not negotiate MPTCP by default, and no data is being sent to the HTTP server over 443, we strongly suspect this activity is scanning for CVE-2026-98432 specifically. The use of residential proxies and RU-based VPN servers suggests that this is likely threat actor scanning, rather than security researchers.  Currently there are no known publicly available remote code execution exploits, but there are several denial of service proof-of-concepts floating around. This code gives threat actors a starting point to begin attempting to weaponize the vulnerability. Building exploits for the vulnerability is reported to be extremely difficult, but several state-sponsored threat actors likely have the resources required to succeed.

My moderately informed midwit take is that I think the reason 'cyber letters of marque' constantly keeps getting re-floated is because the US government has a problem it has neither the time, money, headcount, nor risk appetite to address.  You have a bunch of hostile foreign threat actors hacking into US infrastructure, but not in a way which constitutes an "attack" and that the US would be comfortable responding to with much more than what they're already doing. It's mostly just nuisance stuff like cybercrime & espionage, rather than "attacks" in the military or terrorist sense.  One huge issues right now is that North Korea have basically decided that cybercrime is central to their economic policy, so are encouraging people to join the military and commit crimes for a living.   DPRK's cyber capacity is growing at an unprecedented rate, and the headcount of their cyber force is absolutely huge. Currently they're mostly concerned with stealing cryptocurrency, which isn't not even remotely important to the US economy. But that doesn't mean that DPRK can't quickly re-task their capacity towards something more damaging.  Typically, the solution to unreachable cyber actors who become too problematic is for the state to hack them, take all their money, flatten their infrastructure, and then public indict them.  You can't really do that as easily with state-sponsored actors, because launching destructive cyber attacks against a hostile foreign military could be considered an escalation, regardless of what they did to deserve it (unless they did something that met the bar for an "attack" first).  The US government likely doesn't have that kind of risk appetite. If you start wiping out DPRK military systems, they will consider that an escalation, as will their allies, some of whom have some extremely advanced cyber capabilities and an lot of personnel.  The US military's core cyber capacity is not huge, and its extremely fragmented. You have US Cyber Command, which is a decent size, but not huge. Then a bunch of random military units and contractors all over the place.  Already the US is struggling to deal with DPRK crypto theft and remote workers, Iran attacking critical infrastructure, China embedding themselves in everything they can find. The last thing they need is escalation.  I don't think anyone is vying to be the one to pull the trigger on launching into a direct confrontation with with several extremely powerful cyber actors. I know people love to do the whole "US #1. Most powerful military on the planet" thing. But that hasn't been working out so great for them.  So cyber letters of marque are useful because it allows the US to basically encourage civilians to attack targets for them, increasing US capacity, and also shifting some of the risk off of government and onto civilians.  It's easy to find like 50,000 Jason Borne wannabe goober ass mf'ers who are happy to throw hands at well-resources foreign cybercrime actors, and even hostile state military and intelligence agencies. It might actually even keep the adversaries busy.  It's certainly an idea for the US government, but will likely be a terrible one for just about everyone else, including the US public. It's essentially just a way of turning random pentesters into state-certified cannon fodder, and everyone else just gets caught in the crossfire.  I don't know exactly what would happen if something like that actually gets approved and operationalized, but I just know it's going to be absolutely hilarious in the worst way possible.  Just imagine a bunch of Nessus monkeys at some random pentest mill going toe-to-toe with the MSS, FSB, SVR, or RIGB. The amount of popcorn I'd need for this would exceed the total global corn supply.

"There's interest in bringing back 'letters of marque and reprisal' to counteract the cybercrime that North Korea is committing."  North Korean cyber actors are military and intelligence personnel. If you're gonna go getting yourself into a direct confrontation with a hostile state's military apparatus, I'd say: gl, hf, and make sure you have a decent life insurance policy

A 2017 classic.  My favourite were the images they produced of Anonymous bombing offices, and then their CMO getting into an argument on Wikipedia when their GenV page got flagged for delegation.

I don't think they're necessarily uninformed. If they don't know details people are doing their job well in cybersecurity.

One of the problems the industry has is decades of crying wolf about everything, cyber pearl habour etc.  The result is most people don't care.  And that's okay.

I did ICS sec for a good while and all the time we'd get Siemens etc saying 'turn off AV, firewalls etc' otherwise they wouldn't do the install.  When pushed back, they'd come back with 'it's fine, we run nuclear power plants like this'.  

It's like, my guys, that is not as reassuring as you think.

i love the holiday season.  and greggs.

I'm not a victim, just responding to "despite your habit of pretending so".

I wasn't dismissing your experience, FWIW.  I'm sure external IR is busy.  I'm just offering a wider context view where I don't think there's reasons for folks outside to be concerned.

Don’t get me wrong - raw automation, great, do it. You should have done it fifteen years ago.

제공해주신 위협 인텔리전스 데이터를 분석한 결과입니다.

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 공격은 LLM을 활용한 공격 자동화 및 LLMJacking과 같은 클라우드 자원 탈취가 급증하고 있으며, 공격자들은 AI 에이전트를 활용해 침해 후 단계(post-exploitation)를 자동화하는 추세입니다 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/data-privacy/3am-affiliate-ai-loops-european-school-attack)). 또한, 공급망 공격의 일환으로 보안 도구의 업데이트 채널을 하이재킹하여 백도어를 유포하는 방식이 확인되었습니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/cpguard-update-channel-hijacked-to.html)). 더불어, 130만 대 이상의 Android TV 셋톱박스를 감염시킨 대규모 봇넷 사례처럼 IoT 기기를 프록시로 악용하는 위협이 지속되고 있습니다 ([Krebs on Security](https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/11/tech-firms-dismantle-botnet-that-turned-1-3m-tv-boxes-into-proxies/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
*   **Lazarus Group**: Binance를 포함한 대규모 암호화폐 탈취 및 금융 인프라 공격 수행 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/binance-hack-test-attack-paths))
*   **3AM Ransomware**: 유럽 교육 기관을 대상으로 AI 기반의 자동화된 루프를 활용한 랜섬웨어 공격 수행 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/data-privacy/3am-affiliate-ai-loops-european-school-attack))
*   **Leakers$**: 원격 관리 소프트웨어 취약점을 악용하여 공공 빌보드에 부적절한 콘텐츠를 게시하는 등 파괴적 활동 수행 ([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/bugs/2026/11/hackers-put-porn-on-public-billboards-and-claim-it-was-far-too-easy))
*   **APT28 (Fancy Bear)**: NATO 국가의 조선소 및 관련 방산 업체를 타겟으로 한 사이버 첩보 활동 ([bugajski_lukasz](https://twitter.com/bugajski_lukasz/status/2116938333188178245))

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
*   **KEPCO ES 개인정보 유출**: 더존비즈온 해킹 사고의 여파로 한국전력 출자기업인 켑코이에스에서 주민등록번호 등 개인정보 유출 가능성 발생 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209299))
*   **국가 사이버 보안 체계 개편**: 대통령실의 '사이버 보안 차르' 기구 구성 검토 및 공군 1호기 탑승자 개인정보 유출 사건 수사 진행 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=209298))
*   **C3RB3R 랜섬웨어**: 국내 시놀로지 NAS 사용자를 대상으로 한 랜섬웨어 공격 확산 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5791))

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
*   **CVE-2026-98432**: Linux kernel IPv4 TCP RCE, 심각도 9.8, 즉시 패치 권고 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5792))
*   **CVE-2026-111497**: Node.js Brotli decoder RCE, 심각도 높음, 패치 필요 ([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/96266/))
*   **CVE-2026-109618 / 109619**: PHP RCE (PHP2Shell), 심각도 높음, 광범위한 악용 중 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/))

### 5. IOC 요약
*   **CVE**: 
    *   CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/))
    *   CVE-2026-111497 ([Qualys Blog](https://blog.qualys.com/category/vulnerabilities-threat-research))
    *   CVE-2026-98432 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5792))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
*   **Linux 커널 및 PHP/Node.js 업데이트**: 언급된 RCE 취약점(CVE-2026-98432, PHP2Shell, Node2Shell)에 대한 최신 보안 패치를 즉시 적용하십시오.
*   **클라우드 LLM 접근 제어 강화**: LLMJacking 방지를 위해 LLM API 키 관리 및 클라우드 컴퓨팅 사용량에 대한 실시간 모니터링/알람 설정을 강화하십시오.
*   **NAS 및 외부 노출 자산 점검**: 시놀로지 NAS 등 외부 노출된 장비의 펌웨어를 최신화하고, 불필요한 원격 관리 포트 노출을 차단하십시오.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
*   **점수**: 8.5/10
*   **근거**: RCE 취약점의 광범위한 악용과 AI를 활용한 공격 자동화가 결합되어 기업 및 공공기관의 침해 사고 위험이 매우 높은 상태임.
